sentences.text: This herbivorous dinosaur measured between 4 and 6 meters in length and stood 2.5 meters tall.
It possessed a large, elongated, and flat head approximately 1 meter long with a long, narrow snout.
The animal was lightly built, featuring long, slender arms and hands equipped with a small thumb spike.
Feeding involved using a toothless beak to strip vegetation, which was then processed by wide cheek teeth set in irregular rows.
Estimates suggest the creature reached a length of 5.5 meters and weighed one tonne.
Although it was probably predominantly quadrupedal, it shared specific physical features with later duck-billed dinosaurs.
A Soviet-Chinese expedition uncovered remains in Inner Mongolia near Maortu during 1959 and 1960.
Fossils were located in the Dashuigou Formation in Zizhiqu, Inner Mongolia, China.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as PIN 2232/1, consists of a partial skeleton that includes a skull.
The type species Probactrosaurus gobiensis was formally described and named by A. K. Rozhdestvensky in 1966.
The specific name gobiensis refers to the Gobi Desert.
Originally assigned to Iguanodontidae, it is now viewed as a basal member of Hadrosauroidea closely related to Hadrosauromorpha.
A 2010 study by Prieto-Márquez and Norell confirmed its status as a basal Hadrosauroidea.
It is considered a representative of Hadrosauroidea within Iguanodontia, though its exact relationships remain unclear.
Probactrosaurus lived in Asia during the Early Cretaceous, approximately between 96 and 88 million years ago.
Its time range spans the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
It is debated whether the closest relatives of Probactrosaurus are Equijubus and Protohadros.
